one_month_reasoning: There are two events in the window, which ends with the Oct 30 close because Nov 1 is a Sunday. (1) Q3 2026 results and the Q4 guide, expected Wed Oct 21 after the close. Nasdaq/Zacks show it as 'expected', and it fits TI's 2026 Wednesday cadence; it is not confirmed by TI. The Q3 guide was $5.65-6.15B revenue and $2.23-2.57 EPS. Consensus is $2.42 for Q3 and $2.28 for Q4, with 24 upward revisions and none down in 30 days (16). So a Q3 beat is mostly priced, and the swing factor is the Q4 guide: seasonal decline, pull-ins and rising depreciation. The July beat-and-raise was followed by a 19% slide (8), and Zacks cut TXN to Hold on 2026-09-21 (15). That argues for a mild downside skew, not a directional call. (2) The $1.52 dividend goes ex on Oct 30 (record date Oct 30 under T+1), which lowers the last close mechanically. I have dropped the China anti-dumping ruling as an in-window event: China committed on 2025-11-01 to terminate it, and no ruling has appeared (19). The result is a lognormal with a $290 median (about 1% skew plus $1.5 of dividend below $293.8) and a 12% monthly sigma (42% / 3.5).

fair_value.method: 60% P/E plus 40% FCF yield. P/E: horizon NTM EPS $10.54 (0.25 x CY27 $10.10 + 0.75 x CY28 $11.60 less 5%, then less $0.25 SLAB GAAP dilution) x 24x (core peer median 21x plus a 14% premium) = $253. FCF: recurring 2027E FCF of $7.7B / 912M shares = $8.44 at a 3.3% yield = $256, plus $2.37 of remaining CHIPS receivable, less about $1 of SLAB effect = $258. Blend about $255.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 forward (NTM) EPS $10.54 = 0.25 x CY27 $10.10 + 0.75 x (CY28 $11.60 less 5%) - $0.25 SLAB GAAP amortization dilution; x 24x (core peer median 21x CY27 plus a 14% premium)

inputs_detail.derivation: CY27 is largely visible: 23-25 upward revisions with none down, and price rises enforced on open orders, so I no longer haircut it. CY28 rests on 5 estimates and falls in the window where a 2026 allocation cycle typically unwinds: lead times past 26 weeks and parts on allocation (21), auto restock and pull-ins named on the Q2 call (17, 7), and Goldman (Sell) and Morgan Stanley (Underweight) holding their bearish calls through July 2026 (14). Round 1 cut 7% of the whole blend; I now cut 5% of CY28 only.

Net cash outlay is about $7.3B (33.4M shares x $231 less about $0.4B SLAB cash). Lost interest plus term-loan cost is about $0.30/share after tax, roughly offset by SLAB NOPAT plus early synergies before amortization. Purchase-intangible amortization then gives GAAP dilution of $0.2-0.4 (supervisor's estimate, consistent with the 10-Q terms). I take $0.25 because some of it may be looked through. Close is H1 2027, so the full NTM window carries it.

Core 7 analog/MCU IDM peers (ADI, MCHP, NXPI, ON, STM, IFX, Renesas), all on calendar-2027 consensus: median 20.7x, about 21x. The 10-peer median is 23.0x, lifted by small-cap power names on trough EPS. I give a 14% premium (24x), just under ADI's 25x, for a lasting margin and FCF edge: 61% gross margin, 300mm owned capacity, D&A above falling capex through 2028, Aa3/A+. TXN's CY27 growth is the lowest of the core set and its cyclicality is the same, so I do not carry its current 39% premium (29.1x). Applied to horizon NTM EPS, which by Oct 2027 is mostly CY28.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Recurring 2027E FCF ex-CHIPS $7.7B / 912M shares = $8.44 at a 3.3% yield = $256, plus remaining CHIPS incentives $2.16B = $2.37/share, less about $1/share net SLAB effect = $258

inputs_detail.input: 2027E recurring FCF ex-CHIPS, incl. SLAB financing
inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 revenue of about $24.5B (CY27 EPS +19% on consensus implies revenue about +12%) at a 42% CFO margin (TTM 44.6%, trimmed for normal working capital) gives $10.3B, less $2.5B capex = $7.8B. Less about $0.1B net of lost interest and term-loan cost against SLAB cash flow for the part-year after close.
913M basic at 2026-07-15 and 920M Q2 diluted. Buybacks are slow while SLAB consumes cash, so I raised this from round 1's 905M.

About 30x FCF, a bit above the 24x P/E because FCF exceeds net income while D&A runs above capex through 2028, a gap that is partly temporary. No re-rating credit. The CHIPS receivable is added once as a cash-like asset, not capitalized.
$7.3B net outlay against roughly $6-7B of value for SLAB (EBITDA plus $450M synergies ramping over 3 years, less integration cost). Close to neutral.

bear.story: The 2026 allocation cycle, with lead times past 26 weeks, auto restock, tariff pull-ins and rivals' bottlenecks, unwinds through double-order cancellations in 1H-2H27. Q4/Q1 guides disappoint, depreciation compresses gross margin toward the mid-50s, and CY28 EPS is cut to about $9.6 (after SLAB amortization). The multiple de-rates to about 21x, the core peer median, giving about $200. The China AD duties tail is now small because Beijing committed to terminate the probe. A SAMR delay on SLAB is a nuisance, not a driver.

base.story: Recovery continues into 2027 but growth slows. CY27 lands near $10.1 and NTM EPS is about $10.8-11.0 after SLAB. The multiple compresses from 29x CY27 toward 25-26x NTM as the cycle matures, roughly offset by EPS growth. The dividend (about 2%) is most of the return.

bull.story: Industrial and data center power keep growing through 2027, pricing sticks, and utilization rises with capex down. FCF plus CHIPS collections pass $9.5B, and NTM EPS reaches about $12.5 at 30x as the market pays for the FCF inflection.

comps_summary.peer_range: Basis: calendar-2027 consensus EPS for every name, never stockanalysis 'Forward PE'. US names use Nasdaq/Zacks yearly consensus, with off-December fiscal years time-weighted to CY27 (ADI, MCHP, ALGM, POWI as applicable). IFX and Renesas use MarketScreener consensus calendarized to CY27 against 2026-10-02 closes. Core 7 (ADI, MCHP, NXPI, ON, STM, IFX, Renesas): CY27 P/E 14.6x (NXPI) to 25.0x (ADI), median 20.7x. All 10 including the secondary power names (MPWR, ALGM, POWI): 14.6x to 47.6x, median 23.0x. Forward EV/EBITDA is an estimate (current EV / TTM EBITDA grown by each name's CY26-27 EPS growth): core median 14.0x (8.3x to 27.1x), all-10 median 20.7x. Headline medians are the core-7 figures.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TXN trades at 29.1x CY27 consensus ($10.10) and about 31x NTM, a 39-41% premium to the core median. I apply 24x to horizon NTM EPS. That is a 14% premium to the 21x core CY27 median and sits inside the core range, below ADI's 25x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The persistent factors are structural and visible in filings: an industry-high 61% gross margin, owned 300mm capacity giving a cost advantage that rises as utilization recovers, D&A above falling capex through 2028 so that FCF exceeds net income, $2.16B of CHIPS cash still to collect, and Aa3/A+ credit with net debt of only about 1x EBITDA even after SLAB (18, 13). These justify roughly 10-20%. Against more: TXN's CY27 EPS growth (+19%) is at the bottom of the core set, its cyclicality is the same as peers (2022-24 revenue fell about 30% peak to trough), its multiple compressed late in past upcycles, and SLAB adds GAAP dilution and integration risk. Sell-side outperform calls are not used. I take 14%, the low-middle of the band, because my lane's evidence (allocation-cycle signals, 4 Sell/Underweight ratings into 2026) points to late-cycle multiple compression.

thesis_break_reason: $210 is about 20x my horizon NTM EPS ($10.54) and 21x CY27 consensus, which means no premium at all to the core analog median. It is near my bear case and well below the August 2026 low of about $262. Trading there in a normal market would most likely mean the market sees the 2026 allocation cycle reversing: order cancellations or distributor destocking, a Q4/Q1 guide well below seasonal, or gross margin failing under rising depreciation. Ordinary 37-42% volatility around a $283 base does not usually reach it.

key_uncertainties: Whether the 2026 allocation cycle (lead times past 26 weeks, price rises on open orders, auto restock) is end demand or double ordering that unwinds in 2027
Whether consensus CY28 EPS of about $11.60, from only 5 estimates, survives a possible 2027 cycle peak
Gross margin path as depreciation keeps rising in 2027 while capex falls
Silicon Labs: timing of SAMR approval, the GAAP amortization drag, and integration of a currently loss-making business
Valuation: 29.1x CY27 against a 21x core median leaves room for multiple compression even if the numbers are met
China (about 22% of revenue): the anti-dumping case is dormant under the truce but not visibly closed
reasoning: Skeptic lane, round 2. The supervisor corrected four facts. Consensus CY27 is $10.10 from 28 analysts with only upward revisions (16), not Zacks' stale $9.84. TTM FCF includes $1.18B of CHIPS, not $1.6B, and $2.16B more is still receivable (verified in the 10-Q, 18). Silicon Labs adds about $7.3B of net outlay and $0.2-0.4 of GAAP dilution (18). China committed on 2025-11-01 to terminate the AD probe (19). I accept all four. I also replaced my stale 2025 sell-side bear evidence with 2026 evidence. Goldman (Sell, $225) and Morgan Stanley (Underweight, $255) kept bearish calls after the July 2026 beat. Consensus is only 'Hold', with 4 Sells and an average target of $304 (14). Zacks cut TXN to Hold in September and TD Cowen trimmed its target (15). Trade sources show analog on allocation with lead times past 26 weeks (21), the classic late-upcycle setup for double ordering. On the valuation side, my round-1 peer median (23.8x) was inflated by non-comparables. On one CY27 basis the core 7 analog/MCU IDMs sit at 20.7x and all 10 at 23.0x. So I cut my multiple from 25x to 24x, now an explicit 14% premium. I narrowed the EPS haircut to 5% of CY28 only, deducted SLAB amortization, and added the CHIPS receivable to the FCF method. Fair value moves from $260 to $255: the higher consensus and CHIPS cash are more than offset by the lower peer anchor and SLAB dilution. For the ladder, I keep the median near $284, between fair value and spot plus the dividend. Upward revisions and pricing power make a full mean-reversion to fair value in 12 months unlikely, but 29x multiple compression is the main drag. Sigma is about 36% lognormal, a bit under the 42% realized vol, with a slightly thinner left tail now that AD duties are a truce-breakdown tail rather than a catalyst. Scenarios at 25/50/25 on $200/$283/$375 have a mean of about $285, consistent with the ladder. Limits: IFX and Renesas forward EV/EBITDA are my estimates from TTM EBITDA and consensus growth, and the Q3 date is unconfirmed by TI.
